findings.evidence: upstream/TauCeti/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/TensorProduct/Symmetric.lean:85 `def symmetricTensors : Submodule R (M ⊗[R] M) := LinearMap.eqLocus (TensorProduct.comm R M M).toLinearMap LinearMap.id`; :127 `antisymmetricTensors := Module.End.eigenspace (comm R M M).toLinearMap (-1)`; :92 `@[simp] mem_symmetricTensors : x ∈ symmetricTensors R M ↔ TensorProduct.comm R M M x = x`; :134 `mem_antisymmetricTensors … ↔ … = -x`; :165/:194 `isCompl_…`/`isInternal_…` under the same `[CommRing R] [AddCommGroup M] [Invertible (2:R)]`.
findings.fix: Expose the bridge: `LinearMap.range (antisymmProj R M) = TauCeti.antisymmetricTensors R M` (and the symmetric counterpart), or restate the two iff lemmas as `antisymmProj R M x = x ↔ x ∈ TauCeti.antisymmetricTensors R M` and drop the duplicated right-hand sides in favour of the upstream `@[simp] mem_*` lemmas. Put the bridge in a module that may import TauCeti (as `EpsilonEridani/Mathematics/DataStructures/Matrix/PosSemidef.lean` does) if the Mathlib-namespace file must stay TauCeti-free.
findings.issue: `antisymmProj_apply_eq_self_iff` (217) and `symmProj_apply_eq_self_iff` (226) restate upstream `TauCeti.mem_antisymmetricTensors` / `mem_symmetricTensors` verbatim on the right-hand side, but nothing connects the new projectors to those submodules. Post-PR there are two unlinked public vocabularies for the symmetric/antisymmetric part of `M ⊗[R] M`, and a consumer of the projectors cannot reach `TauCeti.isCompl_symmetricTensors_antisymmetricTensors`, `isInternal_…`, or `LinearMap.trace_symmetricTensorsRestrict_sub_trace_antisymmetricTensorsRestrict`.

findings.fix: Drop `[Nontrivial R]` — derive from `LinearMap.trace_map_self_comp_comm` at `f = LinearMap.id` with `TensorProduct.map_id` and `LinearMap.trace_one`, or case on `subsingleton_or_nontrivial R` as Mathlib's `trace_one` does — and tag `@[simp]`.
findings.issue: `trace_comm` is published with an avoidable `[Nontrivial R]` hypothesis (an artifact of the chosen basis proof), narrowing a general public lemma, and it is not `@[simp]` although it is the normal form for the trace of the exchange operator (its spin specialisations at SpinDecomposition.lean:111,119 are `@[simp]`).

findings.evidence: upstream/Physlib/Physlib/Relativity/PauliMatrices/Basic.lean:180-210 `σ1_σ2_commutator : σ1 * σ2 - σ2 * σ1 = (2 * I) • σ3` and cyclic variants; upstream/Physlib/PhyslibAlpha/QuantumMechanics/AngularMomentum/Basic.lean:59-68 `structure AngularMomentumRepresentation` with fields `comm_xy : ⁅Jx, Jy⁆ = Complex.I • Jz`, `comm_yz`, `comm_zx`, and :323 `Jsq`, :449 `Jsq_eq_smul`.
findings.fix: Expose `⁅spinGen i, spinGen j⁆` (e.g. `⁅spinGen 0, spinGen 1⁆ = Complex.I • spinGen 2` and cyclic), which follow from the existing matrix commutators, and optionally the `PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.AngularMomentumRepresentation (EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin 2))` bundling whose three fields are exactly those brackets.
findings.issue: `spinGen` is exposed in the upstream `PauliMatrix` namespace with only `spinGen_apply` and `sum_spinGen_mul_self`; the su(2) commutation relations that characterise it as a spin generator are absent, so nothing in the API justifies reading `LieModule.casimir ℂ _ _ spinGen spinGen` (SpinDecomposition.lean:132) as a total spin squared, and no consumer can instantiate PhyslibAlpha's angular-momentum API from it.

summary: The new projectors are published with no link to TauCeti's already-canonical ±1 eigenspace submodules of the same flip (whose membership lemmas the new iff lemmas restate verbatim), and with no trace lemma, so the downstream consumer must unfold `antisymmProj` to get a dimension. `trace_comm` also carries an avoidable `[Nontrivial R]`, and `spinGen` is exposed without the commutation relations that characterise it.
